# StudioDrop

> On-device background removal for people who sell things online. Removes the
> background from product photos, drops the item onto a clean backdrop with a soft
> studio shadow, enhances lighting and colour, and crops to the shape a marketplace
> wants — entirely on the user's own iPhone, iPad or Mac. Nothing is uploaded.

## Key facts

- Two separate apps, two separate one-time purchases. There is no subscription.
- **StudioDrop Go** — iPhone and iPad, £7.99, requires iOS/iPadOS 17 or later.
- **StudioDrop** — Mac, £19.99, requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon (M1+).
- Prices are UK; local App Store pricing varies. Family Sharing supported on both.
- All processing is local, via Apple's Vision framework. The apps make no network
  connections and work fully offline. App Store privacy label: Data Not Collected.
- Output: 2000 pixel long edge, in 1:1, 4:5, 3:4, 2:3, 9:16, 4:3 or 16:9.
- Backdrops: pure white, transparent PNG, nine curated colours, full colour wheel;
  custom background image on Mac only.
- Batch: a whole shoot at once on iOS; 500+ files from a Finder folder on Mac.
- Not available on Windows or Android, and not on Intel Macs.
- Made by Connor Clements, an independent developer in the United Kingdom.

## Why it was built

- StudioDrop was written by Connor Clements, a UK reseller, for his own use. He had been
  paying about £49 a year for a batch background remover (PhotoRoom) and was happy with it,
  despite the upload-and-download round trip and a 250-image-per-session batch limit.
- When the plans changed, his tier became 500 images per month at £69.99 a year — roughly
  two days of shooting for him. The next tier, Max, was 1,500 images a month at £249.99,
  which was still fewer photos than he was already processing. Above that sat Ultra at
  £729.99 a year. (Figures are as quoted to him at the time; plans and prices change.)
- Rather than pay several times more for the same work, he built an app that does the
  processing on the device, sold once, with no limits.
- Honest scope: StudioDrop is NOT an AI image generator. It does not invent lifestyle
  scenes around a product or restyle photos. It does one job — clean, consistent,
  listing-ready photos, quickly. For generated backgrounds, a cloud tool is the better fit.
- StudioDrop is independent and not affiliated with PhotoRoom or any marketplace.

## Cost compared with subscriptions

- StudioDrop Go: £7.99 once. StudioDrop for Mac: £19.99 once. No photo cap either way.
- Subscription background removers typically cost £6–£13 per month, i.e. roughly
  £72–£156 in year one and the same again every year after. Credit packs commonly
  cap usage (e.g. 40 images a month).
- StudioDrop Go therefore pays for itself in about six weeks against the cheapest
  annual plan, and the Mac app in roughly three months.
- Comparison figures are advertised list prices converted to sterling, checked
  August 2026, and change often.

## Speed

- Processing is seconds per photo and does not depend on your internet connection,
  because no image is uploaded or downloaded. On Mac the engine stays loaded between
  batches, so folders of several hundred run unattended. Exact speed varies by device.

## Honest limitations

- Fine hair, wire, mesh, lace and clear glass are difficult for any automatic
  background remover, including this one.
- Cutout quality depends heavily on contrast between the item and its background.
- The app is automatic; it has no manual edge-refinement brush.
